name: library compression: find reusable subexpressions with holes that shrink the total description of a program corpus

sources.ref: doi:10.1145/3453483.3454080 (DreamCoder, PLDI 2021; the abstraction-sleep phase) -- identifier resolved; content claim remembered
doi:10.1145/3571234 (Stitch, POPL 2023; the same step as a standalone top-down search) -- identifier resolved; content claim remembered
techne/acquisition/receipts/adapter_qualification-stitch_rust_core-20260911T094436Z.json (0 abstractions on PHASE1_3; leak on ALL_17)
archaeon/producer/campaign_h1h0.py extract_library (Archaeon's repeated-subtree extractor: min_size 3, min_count 2, max_components 8; 0 kept on PHASE1_3)

questions.ancestry: DreamCoder's abstraction-sleep step (T2 content claim) was re-implemented by its own lineage as Stitch (T1-SOURCE), whose Rust core runs on this host (T1-LOCAL). A second, cruder implementation of the same idea exists in Archaeon's repeated-subtree extractor (T1-LOCAL). Two implementations, one corpus, same answer on the legitimate corpus (empty): the same cut-finder that separated MAP-Elites' organs says here that the two agree on WHAT the organ computes and disagree only on how hard they look (holes and arity vs exact repeated subtrees).
questions.mechanism: Given a corpus of programs as trees over a grammar, search for a subtree pattern with up to k holes (an abstraction of arity <= k) that, when every match is rewritten as a call to it, minimises total corpus cost (Stitch: cost of the rewritten programs plus the abstraction body; DreamCoder: description length under the updated grammar, T2). Repeat for n iterations, each time adding the chosen abstraction to the grammar. Output the abstractions and the rewritten corpus.
questions.input: a list of programs in a fixed grammar (s-expressions in the JSON route Techne uses), a max arity, an iteration count; optionally a task id per program (uses across distinct tasks are what count)
questions.output: an ordered list of abstraction bodies with arities, the rewritten programs, and the cost before and after; in Techne's export, a canonical-JSON component_library artifact the Vivarium loader accepts (interface boolean-components-v1)
questions.state: the growing grammar (base primitives plus chosen abstractions). Nothing else persists across iterations. Stateless across corpora.
questions.assumptions: programs share SYNTACTIC structure (Techne: 'stitch abstracts over SYNTAX'; two semantically identical programs written differently share nothing); the corpus is large enough and repetitive enough that some pattern is used more than once across tasks (the utility of a single-use pattern is negative by construction); the cost model (node count or grammar description length) is the cost that matters downstream -- the H0-H5 design warns that a macro name can hide execution cost unless expanded cost is charged (design line 370)
questions.interface: compress(programs: list[str], max_arity: int, iterations: int) -> {abstractions: [{name, arity, body}], rewritten: list[str], cost_before, cost_after}. One call, JSON in and out; the Rust binary is invoked exactly this way (techne/acquisition/checks/stitch_on_h1_solutions.py).
questions.fitness_value: In DreamCoder the learned library made later searches shorter because solutions became smaller under the grown grammar, and it made the recognition model's job easier (T2). In Stitch's reported use the value is the compression ratio itself and the speed of finding it (T2 for the claim; T1-LOCAL for the 6.06x / 70 ms reproduction on the fixture). No value has been observed on a Prometheus corpus: the legitimate corpus compresses by nothing.
questions.failure_landscape: (a) EMPTY on small or non-repetitive corpora: 3 real H1 solutions of 2-4 nodes -> 0 abstractions, and Archaeon's extractor agrees (T1-LOCAL); the organ is inert until the corpus has recurring structure, which is a property of the WORLD, not the organ; (b) LEAK: given a corpus that includes the held-out targets, the chosen abstractions ARE the targets (3 of 3 on ALL_17), and a later search finds each target as a size-1 leaf -- Techne's viv_library_leak fires SOLVES_A_TASK (T1-LOCAL). This is the cheat control that already ran as a defect; (c) SYNTAX-BOUND: semantically equivalent programs in different surface forms are invisible to it (Techne, T1-LOCAL); a canonicalising pass upstream changes the answer; (d) COST-MODEL DEPENDENCE: what counts as 'smaller' is the grammar's cost; a macro that hides a large expansion looks cheap (design line 370, T1-LOCAL); (e) the abstractions' utility depends on the arity cap and iteration count (Stitch's --max-arity=3 --iterations=3 are the documented example values, T1-LOCAL); (f) at scale the search is a top-down pattern search with pruning (Stitch reports upper_bound_fired 658, useless_abstract_fired 492 on the fixture, T1-LOCAL) whose cost grows with corpus size in a way not measured here.
questions.ablation: Removing the organ from H0 is the design's own 'library off' cells (design s357: neither / failures only / library only / both), NOT yet run (T1-LOCAL that they are designed). Damaging it: replace stitch with Archaeon's exact-repeat extractor (no holes) -- on PHASE1_3 the two already coincide at zero, so on that corpus the ablation is unobservable (eligibility count 0). A corpus on which they differ is needed before any ablation number means anything.
questions.decomposability: Yes: (1) the pattern-with-holes matcher (PRIMITIVE) is separable from (2) the utility function (cost-before minus cost-after, a PARAMETERIZATION of the cost model) and from (3) the greedy iteration schedule (choose one, rewrite, repeat: a MECHANISM shared with many greedy set-cover style procedures). Stitch's own stats separate them (worklist steps, utility calculations, pruning rules). Below the matcher is tree unification, trivia.
questions.composability: Any producer of program trees (Proteus's boolean programs are the live one; CA rule descriptions, proof terms, world manifests are candidates) and any consumer of a grammar extension: an enumerator whose prior includes the new names (the recognition/enumeration organ), a mutation operator that inserts library calls, a curriculum that targets tasks a library does not yet cover. The output is typed data (canonical JSON), which the H0-H5 design requires (line 269: a learned library is typed data, never a dynamic import).
questions.human_prior: Intrinsic: a corpus with recurring parts can be re-described more cheaply by naming the parts, and the names change what a search reaches first. Human and arbitrary: that the parts are SYNTACTIC subtrees (not behaviours); that the cost is description length under a grammar (not execution cost, not evaluation count); that abstractions are chosen greedily one per iteration; that the library is a flat list of named functions rather than, say, a distribution over edits. A soup organism has no reason to inherit the s-expression view of 'part'.
questions.control: Positive: the pinned nuts-bolts fixture must yield 3 abstractions and 1919558 -> 316890 (T1-LOCAL, byte-pinned input). Negative: a corpus of programs with no shared subtree (PHASE1_3 is one) must yield 0 abstractions and cost unchanged (T1-LOCAL). Both exist and both ran. Cheap: 70 ms.
questions.cheat: Feed the compressor a corpus that contains the target tasks' own solutions: the abstractions must come out equal to those solutions and a downstream search must solve each target as a leaf. This cheat has ALREADY FIRED as a real defect (ALL_17, viv_library_leak SOLVES_A_TASK, T1-LOCAL), which is the strongest possible evidence that the leak detector can see the thing it claims to see. Any H0 library cell must run this cheat beside it.

alternative_cuts: AMBIGUITY.md cut B: compression is not separable from the enumerator's objective (the cost the compressor minimises IS the enumerator's prior); the pair is one organ
AMBIGUITY.md cut C: the grammar with a prior is the organ; compression and enumeration are two operations on it
